questions.question: 把代码库看成普里高津式的「耗散结构」，会得出什么样的维护策略？
options: 既然熵增不可避免，就接受代码库必然腐化，到时候整体重写即可
建立持续重构之流来不断再生秩序，而不是一次性彻底整理完就放手
集中精力做一次彻底的大重构，之后冻结改动，让系统保持在有序状态
尽量把代码库与外界隔离成封闭系统，减少输入就能阻止熵的增加
questions.explanation: 文章说秩序是一种流而不是状态，只在能量穿流时存在；所以别追求「一次做好就稳定」，要建立持续再生秩序的代谢。一次性整理完就放手的代码库必然腐化，有持续重构之流的才长期有序。封闭系统的熵恰恰只增不减。
questions.question_en: Treating a codebase as one of Prigogine's dissipative structures leads to what maintenance strategy?
options_en: Since entropy always rises, accept that the code will rot and plan to rewrite it wholesale later
Keep a continuous flow of refactoring that regenerates order, rather than one big cleanup and walking away
Do one thorough refactor, then freeze changes so the system stays in its ordered state
Seal the codebase off as a closed system; fewer inputs means entropy can't increase
questions.explanation_en: The article says order is a flow, not a state; it exists only while energy streams through. So don't chase 'build it once and it stays ordered'; build a metabolism that keeps regenerating order. A codebase cleaned once and abandoned rots; one with steady refactoring stays ordered. Isolated systems are exactly where entropy only rises.

questions.question: 按文章对「临界慢化」的应用，下面哪种迹象最说明一个人的身心状态正在逼近临界点？
options: 从小挫折中恢复得越来越慢，睡一觉不够了，周末也缓不过来
工作效率突然大幅下降，在某一天之内就明显地整个崩溃了下来
偶尔遇到一次很大的打击，但很快就恢复了原来的状态
最近承担的任务数量和每周工作时长比上个月多了一倍
questions.explanation: 临界慢化指越接近临界点，系统从扰动中恢复得越慢，这是相变之前可测的预警信号。文章的建议是：当你从小挫折中恢复越来越慢，就该在相变前干预，而不是等到崩溃之后。突然崩溃已是相变本身。
questions.question_en: Applying the article's idea of critical slowing down, which sign best indicates someone's mental and physical state is nearing a tipping point?
options_en: Bouncing back from small setbacks more and more slowly: a night's sleep or a weekend no longer resets you
A sudden steep drop in productivity, an obvious collapse within a single day
Taking one big blow occasionally but quickly returning to normal
Taking on twice as many tasks and weekly hours as last month
questions.explanation_en: Critical slowing down means that near a tipping point, a system recovers from perturbations ever more slowly, a measurable warning before the transition. The article says when your recovery from small setbacks keeps slowing, intervene before the shift rather than after collapse. A sudden crash is the transition itself.

questions.question: 把量子「退相干」当作思维模型，文章推出了一个关于可选性的什么结论？
options: 越早做出不可逆的承诺越好，这样就能避免选项被环境偷偷吞掉
只要自己不主动做决定，所有的选项就会一直完整地保留下去
不必别人来逼，可选性也会随你不断承诺、暴露立场而自行消失
保留的选项越多越好，因为维持开放的选项本身几乎没有任何成本
questions.explanation: 退相干说叠加不只被主动测量摧毁，还会因系统与环境纠缠而自发坍缩。迁移过来就是：可选性会随着你不断对外承诺、与环境耦合而悄悄消失，所以要主动延迟绑定。文章同时说维持选项有成本，只留凸性最高的几个。
questions.question_en: Using quantum decoherence as a mental model, what conclusion about optionality does the article draw?
options_en: Commit irreversibly as early as possible, so the environment can't quietly eat your options
As long as you don't actively decide, every option stays fully intact indefinitely
No one has to force you: options quietly vanish as you keep making commitments and taking public stances
The more options you keep the better, since keeping options open costs almost nothing
questions.explanation_en: Decoherence means a superposition collapses not only when deliberately measured but spontaneously through entanglement with the environment. Translated: optionality erodes as you commit and couple to the world, so delay binding on purpose. The article also says options cost upkeep, so keep only the most convex few.
